supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42 UTC, amy.cole ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-ORC-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\amy.cole\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon records creation of that archive.

At 13:48:11 UTC, WS-ACOLE-01 sent about 51 MB through the proxy tunnel to megadrop-files.com, with only about 8.8 KB in the reverse direction. The destination is not among the approved services listed in the environment context.
The large transfer is attributable to Chrome running as amy.cole on WS-ACOLE-01.
The close timing between archiving the Clients share and the large outbound transfer to an unapproved file-sharing destination strongly supports suspected data exfiltration.

known_telemetry_limitations: The alert describes activity around 13:46 UTC, while the available bulk-transfer records are timestamped 13:48:11 UTC; the records establish a large transfer within the review window, but not an exact 13:46 transfer. (T279-00227, T279-00228)
The proxy record identifies a CONNECT tunnel and byte counts, not the uploaded URL, filename, or payload; Zeek likewise supplies connection-level byte counts. (T279-00227, T279-00228)
The available records do not directly link c.zip to the bytes sent in the later tunnel.
claims_not_established: That c.zip, rather than another file or data, was the payload of the megadrop-files.com transfer. (T279-00192, T279-00227, T279-00228)
The exact contents of the archive or whether the external service received and retained the data.
Whether amy.cole had authorization or a legitimate business reason for accessing or transferring the Clients data.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine WS-ACOLE-01, including c.zip, its contents and metadata, relevant browser history, and file-access records for the Clients share.
Obtain proxy or endpoint telemetry that can identify the uploaded object and confirm the destination-side transfer, and check for related activity by amy.cole.
Verify with the data owner and amy.cole whether the archive or transfer was authorized; consider containment and account-protection steps while investigating.
unrelated_findings: Earlier that day, amy.cole browsed Google Drive through Chrome; these records show browsing, not a large upload, and are separate from the alerted megadrop-files.com transfer. (T279-00009, T279-00010)
VS Code accessed dbeaver.io from WS-ACOLE-01; this is separate web activity and is not evidence for the alerted transfer. (T279-00089, T279-00091, T279-00092, T279-00095)
